newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes end up, lack of buyers.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes end up, lack of buyers.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes rose Tuesday with WTI/Cushing prices, but Alaskan crude differentials stayed flat in a spot market that lacked buyers, traders said.
Buyers shopped for foreign alternatives to Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude Tuesday, with speculation that supplies remained tight on decreased production in Alaska.
"BP's perception is they're tight," a buyer said, adding the next deal would not sell wider than the $1.10 discount done February 11.
One ANS buyer said he considered importing Australian Cossack oil in April for a undisclosed price and volume.
Another refiner looked to buy Oriente crude with a third party.
Meanwhile, a volatile NYMEX energy market also kept buyers wary of doing deals.
Outright prices for ANS rose five cents to $21.30/21.50 a barrel, five cents over Friday.
Prices for Kern River crude remained $12 63/14.63 a barrel, with one leadig producer claiming they would refuse to discount their barrels more than 90 cents under postings.
